notes.title: 1.1 Design Manifesto & Patch Notes
notes.content:
[p]Hey backlanders,[/p][p][/p][p]Today we want to show the (extensive!) patch notes for our upcoming “Clockmaker’s Tools” update, coming[b] September 29th[/b]![/p][p][/p][p]By posting as much information as we can early, we hope we can have a conversation about the changes, and also allow you to prepare ahead of time.[/p][p][/p][p]Since this update brings significant overhauls to several systems, items and skills, we thought it would be valuable to [b]also do our very first Design Manifesto[/b] explaining our reasoning behind each of these changes.
[/p][p]We believe that transparency and communication (as well as us being humble and changing things when we are wrong) are the key for us to make Hell Clock the best game it can be.[/p][p][/p][p]We won’t get into [b]Crafting[/b] in this Manifesto, since we already did a deep dive on it last week, [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1782460/view/515221043692962978"]which you can read here![/url]
[/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1782460/view/515221043692962978"][/dynamiclink][/p][p]So without further ado, let’s get into it![/p][p]
[/p][h1][b]Why are we even making changes?[/b][/h1][p][/p][p]The game’s been out for a relatively short time, and has done well enough in terms of reviews and sales - so why are we making such sweeping changes to the RPG systems?[/p][p][/p][p][b]What we WANT to do:[/b][/p][list][*][p]We want the game’s defenses to matter, and the challenge of building defensive layers into your builds to be fun and satisfying[/p][/*][*][p]We want damage taken and healing to be more of a “battle of attrition”, and less “spiky”[/p][/*][*][p]We want Boss fights to never devolve into boring slogs[/p][/*][*][p]We want more build variety in the game, with more skills and combinations being viable in both campaign and late endgame[/p][/*][*][p]We want our endgame difficulty scaling to be more sensible, and have a stronger foundation for the upcoming Endless Nightmares[/p][/*][*][p]We want the Veteran Campaign to be a bit easier, but Abyss and Oblivion to be much harder![/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p][b]What we DON’T WANT to do:[/b][/p][list][*][p]We don’t want to nerf any already existing builds. Any build that is S-tier now should remain S-tier when the patch drops [i]\[Mark’s note: except for Manaloop, and Silver Bullets+Powder Bag. We absolutely had to nerf those two :( ][/i][/p][/*][*][p]We don’t want crafting to add even more power creep to the game[/p][/*][*][p]We don’t want Boss fights to resort to cheap one-hit kills[/p][/*][*][p]We don’t want S-tier builds to blow through the entire endgame like it’s nothing, leaving you bored and unfulfilled[/p][/*][*][p]We don’t want you to alternate between feeling immortal and suddenly getting one-shot.[/p][/*][/list][p]
[/p][h1][b]Defenses Rework[/b][/h1][p][/p][p]Hell Clock is currently suffering from a common issue in ARPGs: the defenses start sensible enough, but as the game progresses, you become basically immortal - until something suddenly one-shots you. In our game this is happening mostly due to a couple of outliers. The first one was [b]Lifesteal[/b], which was reworked in 1.0.3; the other one is [b]Conviction[/b].[/p][p][/p][p]The issue with Conviction is that it is very weak if used at low values, and game-breakingly strong if invested in. There are currently many methods to get Conviction to the hundreds of thousands with minimal effort, and to [b][i]millions [/i][/b]with a bit more effort.
[/p][p]We are reworking Conviction from the ground up, and here are the major changes:[/p][list][*][p]Conviction is now capped, and the cap starts at 100% of your maximum Mana[/p][/*][*][p]All “Conviction Gain” affixes have been replaced with “Max Conviction” bonuses[/p][/*][*][p]Conviction Decay is drastically reduced and is no longer linear: it decays fast if you are at or near your Max value, and slows down as the ratio diminishes, becoming very slow if you are in the bottom 25% of it.[/p][/*][*][p]Conviction Decay Resistance nodes, affixes and blessings have been slightly reduced across the board, but are still in the game[/p][/*][*][p]The major sources of Conviction (“Conviction from Mana”, the “Closed Body” Skill, and the “Holy Water” and “Mother of Perpetual Help” Uniques) have been reduced to be in line with the new Conviction economy[/p][/*][*][p]Most effects that would grant you a flat amount of Conviction (such as the “Breath Mask” or “Silver Bullets” Uniques) have been reworked to grant you a percentage of your Max Conviction instead[/p][/*][*][p]The UI bar that represents Conviction now makes a lot more sense, being based on your Max Conviction instead of your Life
[/p][/*][/list][p]Our goal with these changes is to stop infinitely-scaling Conviction, but also to make it more consistent at lower values than it currently is. Earning Conviction will be much harder than before, but it will also decay much less, especially at lower values.[/p][p][/p][p]We are also bringing Evasion down a notch by reducing most Evasion sources (as it is currently extremely easy to cap Evasion with minimal investment), and also making it not work against Area attacks and ground effects. Basically any ground effects and any attack in the game which has a ground indicator, as well as secondary area effects from attacks (such as the Headcutter's ground slam) are no longer possible to Evade.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Less Monster Damage, Less Player Recovery[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]The Conviction and Evasion changes, however, are not being made in a vacuum. With both Lifesteal and Conviction brought back in line, we are [b]rebalancing all enemy damage scaling in the game from scratch[/b]. Our goal is to make the damage you take less “spiky”, and more of a battle of attrition, so all sources of effective health pool (EHP) recovery have been reduced.[/p][p][/p][p][b]This is effectively a global increase on “time to kill” against players[/b], combining a reduction in monster damage with a reduction on players’ recovery ability.[/p][p][/p][p]Our goal is for you to see far less deaths where you are brought from full life down to zero in less than a second, and more often see your death approaching as you run out of options and resources instead.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Fixing Boss Lethality: Curse System[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]This brings us to the issue of Boss fights, which are an absolute pain to deal with in ARPGs. The reason for it is the sheer variety of player capabilities that the vast customization of ARPGs allows for: you can have two characters reach the same Boss at the same point in their progression, but one of these builds has 4,000 Life, uncapped Resists, and just a single defensive layer, and can kill the Boss in 50 hits; while the other one can have 10,000 Life, capped Resists, and two or even three layers, but takes 1000 hits to kill the same Boss.[/p][p][/p][p]We want to keep our “no one-hit kills” design ethos, and we also want to make sure that building defenses and a “tanky” playstyle is rewarding; but we also need to make sure that builds that have good defensive layers can’t just sit still and facetank every single Boss while dealing basically no damage, for 5 minutes or longer.[/p][p][/p][p]With these goals in mind, we are [b]implementing the “Curse” system in all Bosses and Unique enemies[/b]. If you are familiar with the Act 3 final Boss, this is the exact same mechanic. 
[/p][p]Every Boss attack will inflict a few stacks of Curse on you, with the more impactful and easier to dodge ones contributing far more stacks. [b]Each Curse stack will reduce all of your Resistances[/b], and can even bring them to negative values. Defeating the Boss/Unique monster will instantly remove all Curse stacks.
[/p][p]This will allow us to tune Boss damage in a way in which any appropriately-scaled character is guaranteed to not get one-hit-killed by any mechanic the first time they get hit. As the fight progresses, getting hit again (especially with the most telegraphed attacks) will make everything hurt more and more, with tankier builds of course being able to resist a lot further, but overall the challenge and tension of the Boss being maintained.
[/p][p]As a small indie studio, complex and intricate Boss fights are the single most expensive thing for us to create, so although we recognize that the fights in Hell Clock are much simpler than what you’d see in a AAA game such as Path of Exile 2, we hope that with a few well-placed changes we can have them do their job and provide a satisfying experience that fits our game’s structure.
[/p][h1][b]Improving Build Variety[/b][/h1][p][/p][p]With survivability out of the way, let’s talk about damage.[/p][p][/p][p]Although the current build variety isn’t terrible for a 1.0 release of a new ARPG - and is bound to increase a lot more as we release all of the Constellations, new Relics and new Skills - we believe it’s far from where it should be.[/p][p][/p][p]If you consider the current meta, the only types of builds that can currently crush Oblivion easily are using at least one of these 3 techs:[/p][list][*][p]Manaloop (as it completely breaks the game with infinite cast speed);[/p][/*][/list][list][*][p]Scaling damage via extreme stacking of Conviction (either with Silver Bullets or Written Promise);[/p][/*][*][p]Stacking ungodly amounts of Projectile%[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]These three things were at least [b]an order of magnitude[/b] above all other options in the game, so bringing them back in line makes everything much saner. It also allows us to [b]reduce enemy Life scaling[/b] from Act 2 Normal onwards, which frankly could get a bit silly.[/p][p][/p][p]As funny as [b]Manaloop [/b]is, it obviously needs to go. We are introducing changes to the Oxumaré Constellation and to Judgement with the goal of disabling looping. Both changes are also positive, since it aligns Oxumaré with its original design goal of reducing larger cooldowns (it was never meant to be a tool to increase cast speed of Spells), and Judgement is also getting more attention (more details on the section below).
[/p][p]We were also worried about how [b]Silver Bullets triggering Powder Bag [/b]made for very dull buildcrafting, as it outperformed every way of triggering PB and was by far the less creative or interesting. Silver Bullets are no longer Physical, and now add Lightning damage to your shots. With all Constellations and Relics we have planned, the Silver Bullets + Powderbag combo will be viable again in the future, but it will take a bit more investment than it did in the previous iteration.
[/p][p][b]Apart from these two[/b] particular cases above, [b]our goal is to NOT nerf any build that is already working and doing well in the endgame[/b]. If you are running Splitshot with loads of projectiles, clearing screens with Mark of the Vulture, and melting bosses with Summon Rosary, do not worry - our intention is not to nerf anything, we are just reducing the damage ceiling of the game and reducing the enemy scaling along with it.
[/p][p]Hopefully this will pave the way for far more build options being viable, even before the introduction of new content to the game. It will also give us a more solid base to work with for future updates, without losing control over our scaling and ending up with Bosses having literal trillions of Life a few months down the road.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]Economy Changes[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]We are also introducing several changes to the Soulstone and item drop economy in general. The current iteration of the Soulstone economy incentivizes players to go back and farm earlier completed Acts instead of going as far as they can on their current Act - especially in Ascension.[/p][p]
Overall, later Acts will always be more rewarding now, with greatly increased drop rates and also with recycle gains from Relics scaling with higher Tiers as well. We are also updating the Campaign drop tables to ensure that Relics from Act 1 can show up as Tier 2 drops when playing Act 2 of the Campaign.
[/p][h2][b]Vertical Endgame Rebalance[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]For 1.1 we are also reworking the scaling of the [b]World Tiers[/b]. [b]Abyss [/b]and [b]Oblivion [/b]should be MUCH harder now, as it was originally intended, and will require well-rolled Relics and optimized builds to complete.[/p][p][/p][p]We understand that the vertical endgame will never feel fully satisfying until we have [b]Endless Nightmares [/b]out, offering a more fleshed out experience. But still, many of you have demonstrated that you are eager to push your builds to the limit and want something[i] right now[/i] that will allow you to do that.[/p][p][/p][p]So for 1.1 we are also [b]introducing a new, final World Tier: Void[/b]. It is designed to be impenetrable to all but the most powerful builds you can come up with, and will yield no Constellation points - its purpose is purely to serve as [b]a temporary pinnacle activity[/b] while we work on Endless Nightmares.[/p][p][/p][p]Void is [b]ridiculously challenging[/b] and completely optional. We do not expect the vast majority of players to be able to clear it.[/p][p][/p][p]After Endless Nightmares is released early next year, [b]we will probably remove Void[/b] and keep only Abyss and Oblivion in the game.
[/p][h2][b]Other Gameplay Changes[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]We have made several other smaller changes that we think need some clarification about our motivations.[/p][p][/p][p]We are reducing all crit bonuses available in the game. This is part of our effort to reduce the overall damage scaling in Hell Clock, but it’s also because Crit felt almost mandatory in endgame, especially with how little investment was required to reach the crit cap (100% crit chance). Again, [b]this is not intended as a direct nerf to crit-based builds[/b], as the enemy Life scaling has also been decreased to account for it.[/p][p][/p][p]We are bringing some underperforming Skills up a notch, to compete with the more popular ones. This includes buffs to Bombardment, Phantom Marksmen, Summon Brute, Passage, Repeater, Matadeira, Old Bell, and a big buff to the Retaliation damage of Closed Body. This is part of the overall effort to increase build variety and creativity.[/p][p][/p][p]Reflexes has been reworked into “Spectral Knives” to provide better QoL as well as more damage. It now works similarly to a Prayer, with its effect always active, and the activation providing a temporary boost to damage, throw speed and knife regen speed. All Spectral Knives Uniques have been revised and buffed. It is also getting strong synergies by having a natively increased Bleed chance and by gaining the “Spell” tag.
[/p][p]Some Unique Relic Blessings have been removed, either to reduce the overall size of Blessings Decks (increasing their consistency over time) or because those effects could get a bit silly (in the case of Northerner’s Belt cooldown reductions, for example).
[/p][p]Judgment has been changed not only to avoid Manalooping, but also to make the Skill more interesting, and its Relics actually useful. The new base cooldown for Judgement makes it less of an “add to any build for free damage” tool, and requires you to make use of its Unique effects to really take advantage of the extremely powerful Resistances debuffs.We’ve also brought its Blessings down a bit, because the insane amounts of Res reduction that could be achieved with Judgement made it auto-include in all builds, which is never a good thing. To compensate for all these nerfs, we are buffing the effectiveness of Judgement for Ailment builds, giving it a more specialized role in the meta (while still being useful for Res reductions for basically any build, just to a lesser degree than previously).
[/p][p]We have also given enormous buffs to two “meme” techs in the game, in the hopes that you will now be able to take them and turn them into hilariously viable builds in patch 1.1.
[/p][p]With the new focus on increasing the “time to kill” on players, all Life draining effects (such as The Sacrificed or Wheel of Death) have been significantly reduced.[/p][p][/p][p]Also to keep in line with the new survivability scaling in the game, most sources of Resistances in the game have been reduced, and capping Resistances in higher World Tiers and Hell Levels will now be an actual goal instead of being basically “free”. Higher World Tiers are also reducing Defenses as well as Resistances.
[/p][p][/p][h1]Full Patch Notes[/h1][p][/p][h3]Gameplay[/h3][list][*][p]Added "Clockmaker's Tools" crafting system to the game. There are 9 different currencies, and some will start dropping from the middle of the Act 1 campaign. Check our [b]dedicated Crafting blog post[/b] for in-depth information about this[/p][/*][*][p]Monster Life and Damage scaling changed across the board. This is an overall decrease in monster Life and Damage scaling across the entire game[/p][/*][*][p]Conviction Reworked: It now has a Max value determined by your Mana. "Conviction Gain" stat replaced by "Max Conviction". Decay is now [i]drastically[/i] reduced, and it decays even less as your current value gets further away from your Max value [/p][/*][*][p]Evasion Reworked: you can no longer Evade area effects. Basically any ground effects and any attack in the game which has a ground indicator, as well as secondary area effects from attacks (such as the Headcutter's ground slam) are no longer possible to Evade[/p][/*][*][p]Boss damage has been reduced across the board, but all Bosses now have the "Curse" mechanic. Getting hit by Boss attacks will inflict stacks of "Curse" that will last through the entirety of the fight. Each stack of Curse makes you take more damage from attacks. The Jailer mini-boss is the only exception and cannot inflict "Curse".[/p][/*][*][p]"Second Wind" has been changed in endgame. Instead of paying 1 point for 100% death protection (as in Campaign), the Oblivion Bell and Infernal Bell versions now give 25% chance to trigger per point. This means Second Wind now costs 4 points instead of 1 in endgame.[/p][/*][*][p]"Clock Seconds" drops are now dynamically adjusted based on how much time you have remaining. Less time on the Hell Clock increases the chances of obtaining Time drops (up to 300%).[/p][/*][*][p]Base Critical Chance reduced from 5% to 4%[/p][/*][*][p]Base Ignite damage increased from 60% to 85%[/p][/*][*][p]Base Ignite duration increased from 5 to 6[/p][/*][*][p]Bleed chance scaling with enemy Life reduced by 50% [i](enemies having large Current Life pools relative to hit damage now impacts the Bleed chance 50% less than before)[/i][/p][/*][*][p]Bleed chance now has a reduction floor of 10%. This means that no matter how much Life your target has, your chance to bleed on hit will never be less than 10% of your listed Bleed Chance. [i](i.e. if you character sheet says you have 50% Bleed Chance, it can never be reduced to less than 5%)[/i][/p][/*][*][p]Blighted attack speed reduction reduced from 20% to 8%[/p][/*][*][p]Player starting base damage increased from 100 to 180[/p][/*][*][p]Life Drain effects now count as taking damage for the purposes of gaining Vigor Stacks[/p][/*][*][p]Projectile Amount Reworked: after reaching Projectile breakpoints, any excess Projectile% left over will be rolled as a chance to get an additional projectile*. [/p][p]*[i]For example, if your Skill shoots 3 projectiles and you have +60% Projectile Amount, it will always shoot 4 projectiles and have an 80% chance of shooting a 5th one on each use[/i][/p][/*][*][p]Relics now yield more Soulstones when Recycled based on their Tier and on how many affixes they have[/p][/*][*][p]Act 2 (in all difficulties and game modes) now has approximately +25% Soulstones gained, +10% Relic drops and +15% Currency drops[/p][/*][*][p]Act 3 (in all difficulties and game modes) now has approximately +50% Soulstones gained, +20% Relic drops and +30% Currency drops[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced bonus chance to find Potions when in low quantity by 25%[/p][/*][*][p]Memory Level's progression curve has been changed to accommodate the changes in the Soulstone economy (in general it will take a bit more Soulstones to reach higher Levels than it did before this patch, but it should take about the same play time due to the increased Soulstone gains)[/p][/*][*][p]Infernal Bell (Ascension) can now only reach a maximum Skill Level of 7 (down from 8), to accommodate for the new +Skill Level items.[/p][/*][*][p]Minor Mana Nodes in Oblivion Bell and Infernal Bell reduced from 75 to 50[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy Barriers are now considered extra Life for the purposes of calculating Ailment thresholds[/p][/*][*][p]Enemies with Barriers are no longer immune to Ailments[/p][/*][*][p]Ignite and Bleed damage now bypass Barriers and deal damage straight to enemy Life[/p][/*][*][p]Enemy Barrier values increased across the board in endgame [/p][/*][*][p]Players' default Loot Pickup Range increased from 5 to 6[/p][/*][*][p]All Summon Damage affixes on Relics and Skill Trees increased by 40% across the board[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3] Quality of Life[/h3][list][*][p]New Feature: "Death Recap" - notes.title: 1.1 Crafting System Preview
notes.content:
[p]Hey backlanders,
[/p][p]We’re super excited to share details on our upcoming Crafting system in update 1.1:[b] Clockmaker’s Tools, [/b]coming [b]September 29th[/b]![/p][p]
[/p][h2][b]Crafting In Hell Clock[/b]
[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/30e3dac20522644ea1435883156fdff4cda13b1d.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]We have two main goals with Crafting in Hell Clock: providing a [b]tool to mitigate RNG[/b] during your progress (especially in Ascension); and providing another[b] fun dimension to item progression[/b].
[/p][p]Designing crafting systems in ARPGs is very tricky. If there’s too much RNG, it becomes a full “gambling” experience where you feel little to no control over the outcome. If it’s too deterministic, it becomes the main path to item progression, and the good-old “kill monster, drop loot” system that we all love so much loses a lot of its value.
[/p][p]What we are trying to achieve is [b]a healthy in-between[/b] that works in the context of Hell Clock’s quirky structure. We don’t want to have a system as deterministic and as in-depth as Last Epoch, for example, but we also want something that gives you a bit more control than in Path of Exile 2 ([i]pre-0.3, that is[/i]).[/p][p][/p][h3][b]How Clockmaker’s Tools Work[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/afc2c2d4f2aae11e220dc441b5dc2c349b6119bc.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]All crafting in 1.1 is done by using special crafting currency called “[b]Tools[/b]”. This currency starts dropping from the middle of Act 1 onwards, with drop rates improving as you progress further into the game.[/p][p][/p][p]Besides dropping fully-usable Tools right then and there, you can also drop [b]Fragments [/b]- which are useless on their own, but if you gather enough of them you can create a usable crafting Tool.[/p][p][/p][p]Using Tools is easy: in your Reliquary back in town, just click on the Tool you want to use to activate it, then click on the Relic you want to use it on - it’s that simple.
[/p][p]There are 9 different types of Tools available in 1.1, so let’s go over each of them:[/p][p][/p][list][*][p][b]Tool of Tinkering:[/b] replaces a random affix on the Relic with a different one[/p][/*][*][p][b]Tool of Enhancement:[/b] transforms a Common Relic into a Magic with a new random affix[/p][/*][*][p][b]Greater Tool of Enhancement:[/b] transforms a Magic Relic into a Rare with a new random affix[/p][/*][*][p][b]Tool of Locksmithing:[/b] locks a random regular affix on the Relic so that it cannot be removed or replaced. Repeated uses of Locksmithing on the same Relic will switch which affix is locked[/p][/*][*][p][b]Imbued Tool of Fury: [/b]imbues the Relic with a special regular affix (Imbued Affix) related to Fury path (Life, Melee Damage, Life Leech, Fire Damage, Physical Damage, etc). Replaces an Imbued affix if there is one already[/p][/*][*][p][b]Imbued Tool of Faith: [/b]same as above but Faith (Mana, Conviction, Lightning Damage, Mana Shield, etc)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Imbued Tool of Discipline: [/b]same as above but Discipline (Evasion, Move Speed, Projectile Amount, Plague Damage, etc)[/p][/*][*][p][b]Corrupted Tool:[/b] unpredictably modifies the Relic, which become Corrupted and cannot be modified further[/p][/*][*][p][b]Divine Tool:[/b] improves the values of all Affixes on the Relic[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3][b]Imbued Relics[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/87327404888748a854dfbf0918ee9cb901448d51.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]With 1.1 we are introducing a new type of implicit affix called “[b]Imbued[/b]”. Rarely, you will find Relics in the world which will come already Imbued with one of the three Paths (Fury, Devotion, Discipline) - but as we’ve just shown, there are also specialized Tools that will allow you to craft these powerful affixes into any Relic you want.[/p][p][/p][p]To allow for even more control of crafting results, the outcome of the Imbuements are different depending on the size of the Relic. For example, a Small (1x1) Relic that is Imbued with Fury can only roll either Life%, Endurance, or Life Regen.[/p][p][/p][p]Combined with the fact that you can re-apply Imbued Tools to Relics as many times as you want to get different results, this helps mitigate RNG significantly.[/p][p]
[/p][h3][b]Corruption[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/6e76ca604357d03358fda077af1c1b84824889aa.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]And of course, no fun crafting system in an ARPG would be complete without the inclusion of the ultimate gambler’s gambit: [b]Corruption[/b]. To truly get your most powerful items to the next level, you can risk it all and apply a Corrupted Tool to them, with volatile results.
[/p][p]No matter the outcome, after applying the Tool of Corruption to an item for the first time, that item will become Corrupted, which prevents any Tools from being used on it (including Tool of Corruption).
[/p][p]Corrupted Tool’s will have a 25% chance to do absolutely nothing besides Corrupting the item.
[/p][p]They will also have a 25% chance to randomize the existing affixes (which most probably will “brick” it, making it useless for your build).
[/p][p]However, there is also a 25% chance that it will improve all of the affixes on the Relic, similarly to a Divine Tool. The intensity of this effect is also random, but it can be as powerful as using 3 Divine Tools![/p][p][/p][p]And finally, there is a 25% chance to add a brand new kind of implicit affix to the item: a Corrupted Affix. These will be extremely powerful, and the possible Corrupted Affixes are also based on the size of the Relic. For example: Corrupting a Grand Relic (4x1) can result in affixes such as “+1 Max Summons”, or “+50% Projectile Amount”.[/p][p][/p][p]Naturally, just as with Imbued Relics, you will be able to drop Relics which are already Corrupted. These will always contain a Corrupted implicit - and if you are REALLY lucky, you can drop a Relic that is both Imbued AND Corrupted.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Why Can’t We Craft on Gear?[/b]
[/h3][p]As some of you may have already noticed, Gear in Hell Clock is not designed to be build-defining. They are mostly base stats and stat multipliers that amplify what you are building with your Relics and Constellations - putting them into the same category of the Bell skill tree.
[/p][p][b]The traditional “Gear” from ARPGs in Hell Clock is, and has always been, the Relics. [/b][/p][p][/p][p]The reason why we went with this system in the first place is because of our game’s unique structure: we want you to put together builds on the fly, very fast, and not grind or trade for specific things in order to be successful.[/p][p][/p][p]Having Unique effects tied to Gear pieces meant you would have to juggle very limited item slots, which naturally decreases the amount of possible combinations. For example, if both “Powder Bag” and “Blunderbuss” were Gloves, you could not have their effect simultaneously in your build.[/p][p][/p][p]This is probably why the Diablo 4 designers chose to have Legendary effects transferable between gear slots, for example - and such a solution would be too cumbersome for a fast-paced game like Hell Clock.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]How scarce will the currency be?[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]Our intention is for the leveling/campaign experience to already offer you a few Crafting options, mostly to help mitigate bad RNG and maybe to offer a few exciting and unexpected “gg” crafts, sporadically. Expect quite a few Tinkering and Enhancement tools to be available, with some Imbued tools here and there, and the Greater Enhancement tools being the rarest drops of them all. Corrupted and Divine drops should be cause for celebration.[/p][p][/p][p]In the endgame (both in higher World Tiers and in the upcoming Endless Nightmares), expect a lot more drops, with a Divine drop still feeling like a “gg” moment. You will be able to spam Tinkering, and spend a few Greater Enhancements every session to fish for those perfect Rares.
[/p][p]In general, if you spend enough currency, it should be relatively easy to get the outcomes you want: you can use Locksmithing until you lock your most valuable affix; then use Tinkering until you get a good enough roll on the remaining ones; then your preferred Imbued to get your implicit. Although these seem like extremely powerful tools ([i]and they are![/i]), the amount of items you have in Hell Clock due to the Relic system is larger than in a regular ARPG, so gathering enough tools to min-max ALL of  your inventory will be a true endgame goal.
[/p][h3][b]See you soon![/b]
[/h3][p][b]Clockmaker’s Tools (v1.1)[/b] is right around the corner, releasing [b]September 29th[/b]. While Crafting is the most exciting feature of this update, it is far from the only one - so stay tuned to our Blog posts and our socials for more information leading up to release!

Cheers,
~Mark and the Hell Clock Team[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Update 1.0.3 - The Performance Patch
notes.content:
[p]Greetings Backlanders,[/p][p][/p][p]We are celebrating one month of Hell Clock's release with our third big patch! This time there aren't that many changes, as we focused on the one thing our community has been most vocal about: performance, performance, performance.[/p][p][/p][p]We have worked very hard [i](seriously, type some "o7" for our coder Murilo)[/i] to make a performance patch that would actually matter and improve your experience in a meaningful way. We have also drastically reduced Load times after the initial one.[/p][p][/p][p]We have recruited some volunteers from Discord to test it out and ensure that we are actually tackling the most pressing problems affecting some high-end builds. So a round of applause to our community members who volunteered their time in the interest of making the game better for everyone: [i]BaZinga, Fatalaris, hardwii, hiragi, Justlfied, Monddoc, Ownage, tetris19023, Tetsuo9999[/i], [i]TheOlBamboozler[/i].[/p][p][/p][p]With all that said, a caveat: [b]this patch is not a magical silver bullet that will resolve 100% of performance issues overnight.[/b] This is a significant push, and we have seen massive improvements to some users, while others are reporting improvements limited to the 15-20% range. So your mileage may vary, and we will keep working on it.[/p][p][/p][p]We have a couple of OG Steam Decks around here, and the performance on the Decks seems to be drastically improved, with the game never dipping below 30 frames, with the exception of some heavy endgame builds that can bring it down to the 15-20 fps range (instead of freezing the game or bringing it down to the "unplayable" 1-2 fps range, as it was before).[/p][p][/p][p]Optimizing performance for PC in 2025 is a nightmare as there's such a staggering diversity of devices and setups out there, each with their own quirks. [b]We will keep working on performance[/b] during the following months, so please report (respectfully) any lingering issues you might be still experiencing in the Steam forums, Discord, and social media. We don't always reply, but I assure you we read ALL of those in a group effort between myself, Lucy, Carol and Mason.[/p][p][/p][h2]Lifesteal is dead, long-live Life Leech[/h2][p][/p][p]The major gameplay change for patch 1.0.3 is a rework of Lifesteal. Originally this was scheduled for patch 1.1 (which will introduce an overhaul of ALL defenses and the enemy damage scaling), but we've seen way too many cases of rookie players equipping a single Lifesteal ring and becoming almost immortal, to the point of accessing areas they were not supposed to yet, and spending 30-60 seconds hitting on a single white mob. It made our eyes bleed, truly.[/p][p][/p][p]We decided to scrap the concept of "turning damage into Life" completely, and have introduced something that makes more sense in the broader systems design of Hell Clock. "Life Leech" is now capped at a percentage of your maximum Life every second, and is not cumulative.[/p][p][/p][p]In practical terms, it now functions basically as an extra layer of Life Regen per second, but to activate this layer you need to cause damage (at least once every second). It benefits Life stackers more than any other build, and also benefits builds which take advantage of Life Gain and Regeneration bonuses.[/p][p][/p][h2]Target Dummy is finally here![/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/83c83bd88613cee15a4ccd5c1c404e620ae57a6b.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]You've been asking for this since release, and we've listened: we have added a Dummy to Quixeramobim, allowing you to test your Skills, builds and rotations before descending into Hell.

The Dummy is currently very simple. In the future we hope to increment it with more advanced features such as DPS meters, the ability to spawn multiple dummies, and being able to spawn them as Rares, Uniques or Bosses, as well as adding Resistances and other defensive effects to them.[/p][p][/p][h2]What's Coming Next?[/h2][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/fd5194f746a992083e6d3d671003f59fc7db4fcd.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Patch 1.0.3 should be our last one before our fist Major one: [b]Update 1.1 - Clockmaker's Tools[/b]. We are currently on track to hit our September deadline, and we are aiming to land around the time of the Autumn Sale (Sep 29th).[/p][p][/p][p]Besides the exciting addition of [b]Crafting[/b], and the much-requested QoL features of [b]Gear Stash[/b], [b]Search/Filter[/b] function and [b]Loadouts[/b], we will also introduce a Defenses rework, and a major rebalance of the entire game to increase build diversity and improve the enemy scaling.[/p][p][/p][p]Stay tuned to our socials and Steam blogs in the next few weeks for more information on [b]Clockmaker's Tools[/b]![/p][p][/p][p]Cheers,
~Mark and the Hell Clock Team[/p][p][/p][h2]1.0.3 Changelog[/h2][p][/p][h3]Gameplay and UI Changes[/h3][list][*][p]Bleed stacks now properly show on HUD[/p][/*][*][p]Lifesteal has been reworked to "Life Leech". Now, instead of converting damage dealt to Life, it recovers a % of your maximum Life per second if you have dealt any damage during the last second[/p][/*][*][p]Changed the Unique Relic effect of "Banner of Faith" to "Double Knives gives +X% Life Leech"[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced the upgrade scaling of the Rare Affix "Critical Hits with Melee Skills recover X% Life"[/p][/*][*][p]Reworked and rebalanced all pre-existing Lifesteal tree nodes and gear/relic affixes to Life Leech[/p][/*][*][p]Changed VSync to Toggle and added FPS Limiting, Anti Aliasing Quality and Shadows Quality to the Options menu[/p][/*][*][p]Moved FPS Limit and Damage View Limit to a new Performance section in Graphics Options[/p][/*][*][p]Added Dummy to the Hub. It is unlocked by default in Ascension, and requires defeating the Merchant to be available in Campaign. The Dummy has 1B Life and is considered a Regular enemy.[/p][/*][*][p]Added Reliquary candle light fix[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Performance[/h3][p][/p][p][b]TL:DR - [/b]Performance has been drastically improved, especially for builds with lots of projectiles, and Load times have been reduced as well. Here are the nerdy details:[/p][list][*][p]Removed Unity collision system from all projectiles and replaced with our own custom system[/p][/*][*][p]Remove Unity collision from all breakables[/p][/*][*][p]Some VFXs now can be reused on reaching the max instances instead of creating moreAdded support to reuse poolable objects instead of exceeding the pool limit[/p][/*][*][p]Added support to limit damage values on screen[/p][/*][*][p]Improved spinning projectile movement function[/p][/*][*][p]Improved audio indexing by GUID performance with local cache[/p][/*][*][p]Improved notes.title: Update 1.0.2 Released: Campaign Rework + New Endgame
notes.content:
[p]Hello Backlanders,[/p][p][/p][p]Today we celebrate 2 weeks of launch for Hell Clock - and what better way to do that than to release a massive update that addresses some of your most urgent requests?[/p][p][/p][p]Today's patch 1.0.2 brings a lot of fixes and changes, but most importantly it adds a new campaign balance and a new Endgame system.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/339b74684ed1f7b40107fc357b25939a3a01bddb.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]"[b]Regular[/b]" difficulty tries to address every single pacing, balancing and difficulty issue raised by our players in the last 14 days, and we think it serves as a great introduction for Hell Clock. Any pre-existing Save files will be considered "Veteran", so if you want to experience this streamlined version of the campaign, you will need to create a fresh new Save file.

Also, when you finish the Campaign, there is [b]no more need for the scary Ascension reset[/b]: you can [b]keep all of your progression from the Campaign[/b] and take it straight into [b]Abyss and Oblivion[/b] - and also collect new item Tiers for your build! While we expect the vast majority of players to be able to clear [b]Abyss[/b], we expect [b]Oblivion[/b] to challenge your build and take your character to the limit. [/p][p][/p][p]Whenever you want to give the challenge of Ascension a try, it has been [b]moved to its own separate save file[/b], and unlocks when you complete the Campaign once on any difficulty.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/cbc16221a95812f76c7e0405b3b7785f5a9fd206.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Also, [b]we understand that testing new builds is currently very cumbersome due to the lack of a Gear stash[/b] of some sort. This is a high priority for us right now, and will come in the next update (check the "[b]What's Next[/b]" section below for more details), as well as QoL features such as a Search/Filter for your storage and skill trees.[/p][p][/p][h2]Changelog[/h2][p][/p][h3]Features[/h3][list][*][p]Added new "Regular" Campaign Difficulty - this is a full rework of the pacing and difficulty of the game, taking into account 2 weeks of community feedback[/p][/*][*][p]Added a new vertical endgame activity for Campaign: "Abyss & Oblivion" - keep progressing your build and items through Hell after the credits roll![/p][/*][*][p]Added a new skill tree for Campaign Endgame: The Oblivion Bell. It unlocks automatically after you enter Abyss for the first time. You will keep all of your Memory Level from The Great Bell.[/p][/*][*][p]"Ascension" endgame is now a separate game mode - you no longer need to give up your Campaign progression in order to Ascend. [b]PSA: If you previously had both Ascension and Campaign progression in any of your save files, you now find TWO separate save files: one containing your Campaign character, and the other containing your Ascension[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Added new Tier 7 and Tier 8 Blessed Gear pieces to all slots, with new art and a new visual for T8 Pajeú (white cloak!). These can only drop in Abyss & Oblivion[/p][/*][*][p]Added new Tier 4 Relics, including Unique versions. These can only drop in Abyss & Oblivion;[/p][/*][*][p]Main Menu/Game Setup reworked and Max Save Files increased from 3 to 6[/p][/*][*][p]New "World Tier Selection" screen added to Benta NPC after beating the campaign, allowing you to freely switch from Normal, Abyss and Oblivion progression[/p][/*][*][p]In-game HUD now displays information about the game world: Softcore/Hardcore, Regular/Veteran, and Normal/Abyss/Oblivion (this is particularly helpful for streaming)[/p][/*][*][p]Added the option to fully respec Constellations (point-by-point respec is coming in a future update)[/p][/*][*][p]Selecting a Blessing of Proficiency for over 1.5 seconds will now display a pop-up that better explains the Global Buff synergies for that particular Skill[/p][/*][*][p]Selecting a Blessing of Foundation for over 1.5 seconds will now display a pop-up that better explains how it shapes the draws of your next Foundation statue[/p][/*][*][p]Selecting a Blessing for over 1.5 seconds when attempting to Banish it will now display a pop-up that better explains the effects of Banish[/p][/*][*][p]Added a new "Delete Save File" flow to help prevent user error when deleting files[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Changes[/h3][list][*][p]Reduced the base intensity of Lightning critical effects[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced the lightning flash from Minister of War's dash skill[/p][/*][*][p]Rebalanced Memory Level progression for endgame: it is now much harder to level beyond 80. [b]PSA: If you had a high Memory Level before this update, you get to keep it, but your first level up will take a LOT more Soulstones than normal to "catch up" to the new balance. It might seem like you are "stuck" and not gaining XP, but just keep playing and it will fix itself eventually.[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Memory Level cap is now 120.[/p][/*][*][p]"Vengeance Mode" bonuses now clearly show as a Status effect in-game[/p][/*][*][p]Elite enemy density adjusted across multiple maps (especially in Act 3) - this is mostly an increase in Rare spawns.[/p][/*][*][p]All Biomes now guarantee at least 1 Cursed Shrine spawn, when relevant[/p][/*][*][p]Increased Summon skill cooldowns for Cursed Nests and Profane Nests in Acts 1 and 3[/p][/*][*][p]Players are now immortal at the Quixeramobim hub[/p][/*][*][p]Oxum Rebalancing: this Constellation was performing way, way above what was intended, so we are taking it down a notch, while boosting its damage output to compensate[/p][list][*][p]Reduced Oxum's Bounty Gold Gain Constellation bonus from +10%\[+] to 7.5%\[+][/p][/*][*][p]Reduced Oxum' Reward Gold Gain Constellation bonus from +30%\[x] to +15%\[x] [/p][/*][*][p]Oxum's Gold Constellation Notable damage bonus changed from Additive to Multiplicative[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Reduced Devotion unlock requirement for Caupé, Iemanjá and Jurupari to 2 Devotion Points. This is intended to facilitate hybrid builds early on, without requiring you to always pick the starting constellations for each Path (Ogum, St. Expeditus, Tupã).[/p][/*][*][p]Toll of the Dead Unique Relic affix now adds 3 seconds of base Cooldown to the Old Bell. The intention is to still allow for crazy Summon builds using Toll of the Dead, but requiring those builds to invest in CDR to make them work, instead of being basically "free" as it stands today[/p][/*][*][p]Endurance and Anti-Magic cap increased from 75% to 95%[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h3]Fixes[/h3][list][*][p]Due to performance concerns, we are temporarily deactivating the "sync" options in the Graphics menu. Honestly, our Graphics settings are currently a bit poorly thought-out, and we intend to revamp them as we shift our focus to improving game performance and stability across the board for the next update[/p][/*][*][p]Damage Numbers performance remains a serious issue that we are looking into, so for now [b]we highly recommend playing with damage numbers TURNED OFF if you are experiencing performance issues. [/b]We apologize for the inconvenience as we are working to fix this as fast as possible[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue with Constellation Devotion Paths being inconsistent and becoming "bricked", requiring Ascension players to restart their worlds[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed inconsistencies in Chest spawns amount, Rare Chest spawn rates, elite density, and shrine amounts across various maps (especially in Act 3). This is overall an increase in spawn rates.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where common and rare chests from all biomes after the Scorched Deeps were only dropping T2 Trinkets on all biomes[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue causing all rare chests in Acts 2 and 3 to drop only T1 Act 1 Relics and T2 Blessed Gear[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where rare chests from Caves onward were not dropping Hell Clock timer increments[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where some ring materials would display with distortion[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where you could click the gravestone in the Hub to access a work-in-progress feature[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed Jurupari the Demon Constellation name, which was incorrectly displayed as Jurupari the Judge[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed regular Impaled enemies from ACT 2 F8~10 wrongly using the Wraith Unique drop table[/p][/*][*][p]We have temporarily removed Vulture spawns from Cursed Shrines as we investigate an issue they were causing[/p][/*][*][p]Saviour's Shield icon has been resized[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where you could not Pause the game during non-intrusive Help pop-up screens[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where some stats would display with a wrong value due to incorrect rounding of floats[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where sometimes when interacting with Cursed Shrines your character could get stuck[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue where the "Reduced Mana Cost" affix would sometimes roll negative values and increase the Mana costs instead[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h1]What's Next?[/h1][p][/p][p]We worked really (REALLY!) hard on bringing 1.0.2 to you as fast as possible, as we recognized a lot of frustration from a part of our community and didn't want them to feel let down. But this is not the last update for Hell Clock - quite the opposite![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/fd5194f746a992083e6d3d671003f59fc7db4fcd.png"][/img][/p][p][/p][p]Our focus is currently on our first Major Update, which we call [b]Clockmaker's Tools (1.1.0)[/b], and our current target date for it is [b]September 29th[/b]. Expect smaller fixes and patches until then, but no new features or significant additions.[/p][p][/p][p]Here's our [b]development priority[/b], in order:[/p][p]1 - [b]Performance[/b], performance, performance. We want to make the game smoother and more responsive for the majority of players, regardless of how many effects they have flying on the screen at once.[/p][p]2 - QoL for items and skills, including a [b]Gear Stash[/b], [b]Loadouts[/b], and a [b]Search Filter[/b] for the Reliquary and the skill trees.[/p][p]3- Improving the [b]design of Defenses[/b] and the overall damage curve of the game. Right now in the late game it feels like you are either immortal or getting 1-shot, which is a terrible feeling in any ARPG, so we want to fix that.[/p][p]4 - Adding [b]more Constellations and Relics[/b], focus on enabling new and varied builds.[/p][p][/p][h2]PSA: Hell Clock Tools available[/h2][p][/p][p]To the more crafty members of the community: if you want to create tools, build planners, wikis, etc., we have created a GitHub repository where we're exposing a lot of game data, including everything that has to do with Blessings and Skill Trees. In the near future we will also include Drop Tables.

You can access it here: [/p][p][url="https://github.com/RogueSnail/hellclock-data-export"]https://github.com/RogueSnail/hellclock-data-export[/url][/p][p][/p][h3]
Thank you!
[/h3][p]If you have stopped playing the game since launch due to the Campaign pacing and/or the Ascension endgame, we invite you to revisit the game and renew your feedback. We have listened to you, we have made significant changes, and we are willing to make more if that's what the community wants.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for your incredible support so far! You are making the future of Hell Clock brighter and brighter, and we are looking forward to witnessing just how far we can take this game, and how much better it can be as we keep improving it - together!

[/p][p]
Cheers,[/p][p]
~Mark and the Hell Clock team[/p]

notes.title: Major Update Incoming: Improving Progression and Endgame
notes.content:
[p]Greetings, Backlanders![/p][p][/p][p]We are celebrating one week of release for Hell Clock, and it’s been an incredible ride so far! You have blown us away with your support, and we couldn’t be more grateful.[/p][p][/p][p]Today we’ll talk about the two most important pain-points the community has been reporting: the pacing/balance of the campaign; and the endgame.[/p][p][/p][p]If these are not what YOU are interested in, we invite you to check out our “State of the Game” post from last week, as I believe it is very much still representative of all of the issues that we plan to fix in the coming weeks.[/p][p][/p][p]So with that out of the way, let’s begin!
[/p][h2][b]Campaign Pacing / Progression Balance[/b]
[/h2][p][/p][p]As we said in [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1782460/view/535482620603007178?l=english"][u]State of the Game[/u][/url], the feedback about the campaign balance caught us a bit off-guard. In hindsight it is pretty obvious, but we got “tunnel vision” in the months leading up to release and ended up with a progression balance aimed to please only die-hard ARPG nerds such as myself, to the detriment of the wider audience.
[/p][p]This is our mistake, and we have learned from it. It is not the fault of the player. Our game should offer a reasonable space for learning the systems, while at the same time being an entertaining experience without hours and hours without meaningful progress.
[/p][p]Ideally, we want to turn all of you into huge Exile-like nerds. So here’s our evil plan to achieve that:[/p][p]
[/p][h3][b]Regular and Veteran Modes[/b][/h3][p][/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfwtfF5GoQi79j6zXvkOURzzDdR9HiZB4jwZTUozz-GXGSihQ-XqunsTXBRRPFrGV1fta_yFZSRmkJhiWlSWdWR6eBZcC7_4DXA3bgmh0yYOPV2YCO_rP7ylGLRtK5-dNVJrzzWXg?key=-nh-X5jckImUKx-hvQ4i1w"][/img][/p][p]When creating new save files, you will be able to choose between two difficulties: [b]Regular [/b]and [b]Veteran[/b]. These are fundamental changes to the campaign structure and pacing, so you will not be able to change this after the game has started (similar to Softcore/Hardcore).
[/p][p]To design [b]Regular [/b]mode, we went through (almost literally!) ALL of your feedback, watched dozens of gameplay VODs, and I personally spent the entire weekend tweaking it.[/p][p][/p][p]This is a [b]MAJOR overhaul of campaign pacing and enemy scaling[/b] that we hope will address most - if not all - of your gripes so far.[/p][p][/p][p]But what if you enjoyed the game as it is today? Do not worry, the “Veteran” difficulty is basically the current balance, relatively untouched. For technical reasons, any existing save file when this Update releases will be considered a “Veteran” save file. You will need to create new games to experience the new “Regular” mode. The two experiences are way too different for it to be a “toggle”.[/p][p][/p][p]Speaking of toggle, “Vengeance Mode” and “Relaxed Mode” will still function exactly the same as they do now. You can combine all of these options in any way you want: do you want to play a Hardcore Regular run with Vengeance Mode and Relaxed Mode turned on? You can do it![/p][p][/p][p]As we said before, this is YOUR game, and the only “right” way to play video games is to have fun.[/p][p]
[/p][h2][b]New Endgame Systems[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]In the months leading up to release, we’ve played Hell Clock internally with a mostly “ephemeral” playstyle, mostly not hoarding Relics and with a focus on the reset-heavy rogue-like nature of “[b]Ascension[/b]”.

After release, we have discovered that the majority of players actually play it much differently: a LOT of you enjoy collecting everything, grinding it out, upgrading all Relics and hunting for those perfect rolls to perfect your builds.
[/p][p]While this also sounds obvious in hindsight (since these are staple things of the ARPG genre) we actually underestimated our own game and thought that people would not be as interested in putting so many hours into Hell Clock’s progression.[/p][p][/p][p]At the same time, while Ascension feedback has been very positive for people who actually were onboard with the concept, the majority of players are not even willing to give the game mode a try, and you have told us so loud and clear: [b]you want a more “traditional” endgame, you want to push your builds to the limit, and you don’t want to lose any progress while doing so.[/b]
[/p][p]We heard you, and we’re already working hard on it! We were also not THAT naive - we knew we were trying something risky with Ascension, so we were already prepared to move very fast and change things around in case it wasn’t well-received.[/p][p][/p][h3][b]Ascension is moving to a new Save File[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]If you’re particularly observant, you may have noticed something in the previous screenshot: [b]Campaign [/b]and [b]Ascension [/b]were different things.[/p][p][/p][p]When this Update launches, we will separate Ascension completely from your main Save file to avoid any confusion. After you beat Campaign once with any save files (whether it’s Regular or Veteran) you will unlock Ascension mode, but it will be a completely separate experience that will live in its own Save file.
[/p][p]And of course, all of the customization options from the Campaign are still available: you can play Ascension in Regular or Veteran difficulties, HC/SC, Relaxed mode and Vengeance mode.[/p][p][/p][p]We are also [b]increasing the max save files in the game from 3 to 6.[/b] Any existing save files which contain both Campaign and Ascension progression will be split into two separate ones when the update releases.
[/p][p]We believe this is the right choice for Ascension moving forward. 
[/p][p][i]Speaking as Mark: I am personally very invested in Ascension, and the new Endgame options and Save file separation will allow me to cater this game mode fully towards its audience, which will probably be more niche. This will allow me to do very creative and crazy things with this mode without worrying about alienating the wider audience. Think of this going forward as our own little “Ruthless Mode”, and I personally look forward to building it with you![/i][/p][p]
[/p][p][b]Coming NEXT WEEK: [/b][/p][h2][b]Abyss & Oblivion + New Skill Tree[/b][/h2][h2] [/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/d24e6716022d066fad8568c7cffd5887d84ee50f.png"][/img][/p][p]The first new Endgame system we want to introduce is called “[b]Abyss & Oblivion[/b]”. If you have played Diablo 2, these will basically be our “Nightmare” and “Hell” modes. If you are unfamiliar with this concept, you can think of it as a “New Game+” and “New Game++”.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Abyss [/b]and [b]Oblivion [/b]will allow you to venture beyond Act 3, keeping [b]all of your existing progression[/b]. While we expect most players to be able to complete Abyss, be warned that Oblivion will test you: only the best builds and most hardened Backlanders will see the end of this journey.
[/p][p]You will gain 4 Constellation points when you enter Abyss for the first time, and you will also find 24 additional Cursed Shrines scattered throughout Abyss and Oblivion, providing you with a[b] total of 38 Constellation Points[/b] for your late-endgame builds.
[/p][p]And yes, we will add full [b]Constellation re-spec[/b]![/p][p][/p][p]We will also introduce a new Skill Tree called “[b]The Oblivion Bell[/b]”. As soon as you enter Abyss for the first time, it will fully replace the regular Bell from the Campaign. The Oblivion Bell will offer much deeper progression and customization options for your endgame adventures.[/p][p]
Here’s the breakdown for Abyss and Oblivion:
[/p][p][b]Abyss[/b][/p][p]* Bosses and Survival events no longer freeze the Hell Clock[/p][p]* Bosses have new Mechanics[/p][p]* Uses endgame Drop Tables[/p][p]* New Dangerous Affixes added to Elites[/p][p]* -25% to all Resistances[/p][p]* New enemy scaling[/p][p]* +12 total Constellation points via Cursed Shrines[/p][p][/p][p][b]Oblivion[/b][/p][p]* Even harder enemy scaling, will really test your characters[/p][p]* -50% to all Resistances[/p][p]* Elites have one additional Dangerous Affix[/p][p]* Bosses have an Enrage timer[/p][p]* +12 total Constellation points via Cursed Shrines

Although Abyss & Oblivion will be fun to play through, they do not represent the full vision of Hell Clock’s new vertical endgame. This is why we can’t leave before giving you this following sneak peek:

[/p][p][b]Coming FREE In 2026: [/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/b5e556607eb9f6a3a1cb9a21ce38e5d9b9891ac3.png"][/img][i]"Quem nunca teve um pesadelo... essa noite vai sonhar com Tiriri..."[/i][/p][p]
[/p][p][b]Endless Nightmares[/b] is a mapping endgame, done in the Hell Clock style.[/p][p][/p][p]Cleanse the Nightmares and restore order with the guidance of Exu Tiriri, an Umbanda spiritual entity.[/p][p][/p][p]A new image of Exu Tiriri will be added to the hub at Quixeramobim after you beat the Campaign. Interacting with it will let Tiriri guide you through your very own custom [b]Nightmare[/b]. [/p][p][/p][p]You will take your picks between randomly-generated Shards of Nightmare in a sequence. This will create [b]a new 21-Floor Dungeon[/b], and your decisions have shaped its dangers and rewards. Fully clearing Nightmares will unlock higher tier ones, up to T16 - see how high your build can push![/p][p][/p][p]Endless Nightmares will take advantage of the upcoming [b]endgame-exclusive[/b] [b]Biomes [/b]and maps we’ll be making for [b]The Cursed War[/b] to offer a deeply replayable and customizable experience, with randomly-generated dungeons shaped by your decisions.[/p][p][/p][p]We don’t want to spoil this mode too much, as it is still a few months away, so stay tuned for more Endless Nightmares previews in the near future![/p][p]
[/p][h2][b]Thank You![/b][/h2][p][/p][p]This is it for now! [/p][p][/p][p]To reiterate: ALL of these changes (except for Endless Nightmares) [b]are coming NEXT WEEK in patch 1.0.2[/b]. We can’t give an exact day yet because it will depend on QA testing and debugging, but we are aiming for the beginning of the week rather than the end.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you so much for supporting our game. The main reason why we’ve been able to react so fast is that the majority of your feedback has been very clear, helpful and respectful. It helps a lot when the community tells us exactly what they want, as it fills us with confidence and motivation to make the changes.[/p][p]
Hell Clock is just beginning, and we look forward very much to how we’ll build upon this foundation together over the coming months.[/p][p]
Cheers!
~Mark and the Hell Clock Team[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: Update 1.0.1 and State of The Game
notes.content:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/e5a08de1b97f9b4e2d0dfd2521cc411003e5aa38.png"][/img]  Hey everyone,  It's been 48 hours since Hell Clock 1.0 was released, and we are deeply, deeply grateful for the results so far. Your feedback has been very positive, critics have been unanimously praising the game, and it has been the fastest selling game of our careers.  Does this mean we get to kick back and enjoy a well-deserved vacation? Quite the opposite! We're more motivated than ever to work and make the game better as fast as possible. We are a very small team but we love this game and are pouring our hearts and souls into it, and we hope that it will show over the coming weeks.  We have been trying to read every forum post on Steam and Reddit, every Discord conversation, every review, every video and stream, and trying to figure out how to make this game better for you. Let’s talk about that.[/p][h2]
[b]State of the Game[/b][/h2][p][b] [/b]Every major patch in the future will be accompanied by a “State of the Game” blog post such as this one. These will be opportunities for us to check in with the community and see if we are in sync with one another. Are we seeing the same issues? Are we out of touch? You tell us![/p][h3]
[b]Explaining Game Mechanics Better[/b]
[/h3][p]We have not been doing a perfect job at clearly communicating all of the game mechanics and systems in-game, as we should. Today we have added improved feedback for Relic Upgrades, a new Loading Tips system, and full descriptions in-game for all Ailments and how they work.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/65deebbc752b0dfe28457cd72fae158cf1c76a2d.png"][/img][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/52135bbb2adca0b884870c890cd3fb5da6958513.png"][/img]But there is still more to do. We have in the pipeline an overhaul of the Blessings of Foundation screen (the Gold upgrades mid-run), making it clear how this system works and how you can manipulate it in your favor.

In the future we plan to also communicate Skill synergies (“Global Buffs”) better, and also offer a “Game Help” feature in-game that serves as a “Manual” of sorts and goes over things such as how Multiplicative/Additive bonuses work, and more advanced concepts as well.

In the meantime, you (yes, you!) have taken matters in your own hands and created a community Wiki for Hell Clock! It is not fully fleshed out yet, but there’s already a lot of stuff, including all of the calculations and RPG stats in the game.

Check it out here: [url="https://hellclock.wiki.gg/"]https://hellclock.wiki.gg/[/url][/p][h3]
[b]Introducing Vengeance Mode [/b][/h3][p][b]
[/b]Our release has attracted a larger audience than we expected, and with it came different types of players and different expectations. While the Demo had a majority of players who were build-tinkerers and PoE-nerds like myself and others in the Hell Clock team, the 1.0 launch attracted players from the Action-Roguelike camp, and our game is failing to meet some of their expectations.

Those of you who have been following us since the Beta in December know what our philosophy is: this is YOUR game, the players. Our vision is clear and we will always follow it, but we will not force you to play the game our way. If we can offer more customization, more accessibility options, mod support, anything to make sure you can have fun the way YOU want to, we will. That’s how “Relaxed Mode” was born, for example.

Players who are not fans of the Exile-like genre (yet!) have been disproportionally affected by our game’s opacity in some systems, and the result of that has been that they are grinding through the same areas again and again, and eventually burning out of the game.

Hell Clock is NOT designed to be a grindy game, and it is bad design to punish players who may be new to the genre with no clear feedback as to what is wrong in their builds.

This is why we are introducing Vengeance Mode. Similarly to Relaxed Mode, this can be turned on or off at any point. If you don’t care that much about all the “min/maxing” and just want to experience the combat, progression and lore of Hell Clock without having to stop and grind for hours on end, this mode was designed for you.

In Vengeance Mode, damage dealt is increased while damage taken is reduced. With every failed run, these effects are increased to make your next run even more powerful. 

Regardless of being an ARPG player or an Action-Roguelike player, you are now a Hell Clock player - this is YOUR game. Use Vengeance Mode. Don’t use it. Turn it on when you feel like the game is dragging. Turn it off when you feel like you want to dig deeper into the build-crafting. The only correct way to play videogames is to have fun.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/373a0a868a155d533d6a0ed04fabd4040b60e8e0.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Most Needed Quality-of-Life  [/b]
[/h3][p]As you have been spending more time with Hell Clock, a few key quality of life features have risen to the very top of our lists. Although these are not part of this 1.0.1 patch, they are high priority and will be implemented as soon as possible:[/p][list][*][p]A “Search” function for the Stash and Constellations, filtering and highlighting items based on what you are looking for;[/p][/*][*][p]A “Loadout” feature to quickly swap between builds;[/p][/*][*][p]Improved “Banish” options to have more control over your Blessing draws;[/p][/*][*][p]A “Blessed Gear Stash” to facilitate experimenting with builds;[/p][/*][*][p]The ability to Respec your Constellations both in Campaign and in Ascension;[/p][/*][/list][p]Do you agree with this prioritization? Do you think there’s something more important that should be added before any of these? Please tell us![/p][h3]
[b]State of Ascension Endgame[/b]
[/h3][p]The game has only been out for 48h and it’s still the middle of the week, so the majority of you haven’t reached Endgame yet, so we are still very much in “observation mode” and listening in to all upcoming feedback. 

For those who have already reached Ascension, the feedback has been mostly positive, but we already observed a consensus: Ascension runs are dragging out a little too long.

Next week we plan to experiment with a faster Ascension loop, with 5-run chunks instead of 7-run as it stands right now. Drop rates and rewards will be accelerated, so you should experience the same depth of build progression, but it will take 30% less of your time.

We expect upcoming features such as all Constellations, new Unique Relics, Crafting and the endgame-exclusive Biomes/enemies to go a long way towards improving the replayability and enjoyment of Ascension. But in the meantime, please keep the feedback coming, as we’re sure we can make it much more fun together even before all of the extra content is released.

[/p][h3][b]Performance and Technical State[/b][/h3][p][/p][p]We are aware of performance issues in late game, particularly with some builds that spawn a lot of projectiles and effects. We are working hard on fixing those as fast as possible, and will have more to share soon.

In the meantime, if you are experiencing these performance issues, we recommend you turn off Damage Numbers, since they are bugged and causing significant frame drops in some cases. Also, turning the “Flashing Effects Intensity” slider all the way down can help as well.

Hopefully some of you who are experiencing these issues can gain enough frames by taking these measures to have fun until we are able to fully resolve the problem. We thank you for your patience.

We are also aware of issues with Loading times. We have already fixed one of them, but there is more work to be done and we hope to have more fixes up soon.

For those playing on Steam Deck, some text can be uncomfortably small. This is harder to fix than it seems, as some screens will need a code re-work to allow for text scaling. We don’t have a date estimate yet, but this issue will be fixed.[/p][h3]
Update 1.0.1 Patch Notes
[/h3][p][b]Gameplay[/b][/p][list][*][p]New Feature: Vengeance Mode[/p][list][*][p]You can toggle Vengeance Mode ON/OFF at any point;[/p][/*][*][p]Vengeance mode increases damage dealt and reduces damage taken when activated;[/p][/*][*][p]Every failed run increases the effect of Vengeance, making Pajeú more powerful;[/p][/*][*][p]Turning Vengeance Mode off will “save” the accumulated bonuses for when you activate it again, but you won’t accumulate more bonuses if you fail a run with the mode turned off;[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]New Loading Tips system added to the Loading screens.[/p][/*][*][p]Added improved tooltip descriptions to all Ailments in the Character screen.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced the base price of purchasing Stash Tabs from 1000 to 200 Soul Stones.[/p][/*][*][p]We have limited the amount of Summons and Projectiles that enemies can conjure at one time.[/p][/*][*][p]Reduced Ghoul (ranged zombies) projectile damage by 50%;[/p][/*][*][p]Red Portals now provide Shrine Boons of XP and Gold gain for 30 seconds after you enter them.
