notes.title: Deep Dive: Ascension Endgame
notes.content:
[p]Hey Clockmakers,[/p][p][/p][p]We’re happy to announce that “Ascension” - our first endgame system for Hell Clock - will be available in Beta version for everyone when the game launches next week on July 22nd.[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="R1ctzop0GDE;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Hell Clock’s blending of ARPGs and Roguelikes is very new and we basically had no frame of reference when developing this system. So we feel the endgame will benefit significantly from having real players (that’s you!) having a go at it and giving us feedback.[/p][p]
We expect Ascension to be fully polished by the time our first expansion drops in early 2026 (more to come on this). Keep in mind that the endgame will be FREE if you own the base game, and NOT pay-walled behind the expansion purchase. Any and all content or features related to it that we create in the future will ALWAYS be free.[/p][p][/p][h1][b]Ok, but what even IS Ascension anyway?[/b][/h1][p]
If the campaign is very much a “rogue-lite” (that is, you gain meta-progression that helps you advance further and further on each run), Ascension is closer to an actual “[b]rogue-like[/b]”, but in a very unique way.[/p][p]
In a nutshell, Ascension is a complete reset of your game world, like a fresh League or Season in an ARPG. You lose all of your acquired Levels, Relics, Gear and Soulstones and start a new Endgame run from scratch. You customize the difficulty and mechanics of your new world via a new Skill Tree, and try to beat it with a limited amount of Runs, trying new builds, Relics and Constellations as you go.[/p][p][/p][p]Let’s look at each part that makes up Ascension in more detail, shall we?[/p][p]
[/p][h2][b]Custom Difficulty: Penances
[/b]

[img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXfBMqKOHc5ZdNz5Q5NJjLiWT8jkdq2z-_WDbpvh3B1EZWvfLUDYYgG8ZW2CC0frqiYViUamlqykcgpfWdpi2uIET6Hx3UBADPPM6iUJ4PBIk-29PN_6OPi58jDt5VkshGgBBFTx?key=VYjU1aVjpAbSZisEetooWg"][/img][/h2][p]After completing the campaign for the first time, you can start your first Ascension. You will also be able to toggle a “Skip Campaign” button on new save files if you want to.[/p][p][/p][p]You start by choosing your difficulty level by activating Penances on the Ascension Tree. Penances are modifiers that make the game harder: faster enemies, new Boss mechanics, reduced  Resistances, and much more.[/p][p][/p][p]Each Penance you activate will raise your overall difficulty level, which we call your “Hell Level”, with tougher Penances being worth more points. At first you will only be able to challenge yourself up to Hell 10. Beating Hell 10 will allow you to try Hell 25, and then finally Hell 35, which will be our current maximum for the Beta. The final version of Ascension will allow up to Hell 100.[/p][h2]
[b]Step Into Hell[/b][/h2][p]
After choosing the difficulty of your new world, you step into it, but things are not the same as before.[/p][p]
All Skills are available from the start, as well as all of the NPC services at your hub.
[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXcKXHgnr29H8FsDQiHBpQFlOf7j4itdXvAnflSXtBmwXxDvAd1o_CqcXkRwWJbgtAZ9Xze152xg6ex69UmrGBjmY9HvIoLMUZJnyEEdFVPx1Qsr2UDZI4CME_W6zN3EyNxttiU2lw?key=VYjU1aVjpAbSZisEetooWg"][/img][/p][p]The Great Bell of Canudos is replaced with an endgame version, called “The Infernal Bell”.[/p][p][/p][p]You will notice a new element on your game’s interface: there is now a Run counter below your mini-map! Unlike the campaign, where you could farm and gain meta-progression to your heart’s content until you eventually beat the game, in Ascension you have a limited number of times you are allowed to descend into Hell.[/p][p]
[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXe45Qq8lEYsERzGMlIPEuh1blM1Xg3l-N2ZyvrANvv3YwB1MyqbRl4wHqdpnUgLH8UJ-yTAyz5Vyk08BYYS0OG-NR7eiCOu_G1jbJds9RXaHEe1VKupYBStgFOymZye2vAc1xnpEA?key=VYjU1aVjpAbSZisEetooWg"][/img][/p][p]This means that every decision counts, and not being able to farm turns ARPG progression into a puzzle where you must spend your time and resources wisely and adapt your build by taking advantage of lucky drops, while using resources such as Constellations and The Infernal Bell to make up for stats that might be lacking from your current Gear and Relics.[/p][p][/p][p]If you can’t beat all three major Bosses in Ascension before your Runs counter is depleted, your Ascension has failed and you must start again. At any point you can also simply talk to Benta at your hub and start a new Ascension (this is also the only moment when you can make changes to the difficulty and active Penances).[/p][h2]
[b]Constellations and Devotion Paths[/b][/h2][p]
Although Hell Clock doesn’t have a strict “class” system, the Constellations (via the Devotion Paths) fill that role, a little bit.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdZxhjBlBvw9WJbbgMidyOQ8PhWwJnGYI8MrvnYPbdv4CfMlILRpuH4z9oCHMRsUnMa_x75el-kZ9oSRGnb7hIJcKaIHuqBDTAoaM34wzzdCFVIYI03hQKjGAFMg8-pSE_nCLGf?key=VYjU1aVjpAbSZisEetooWg"][/img][/p][p]
Our Constellations system takes a lot of ideas that you might have seen already in Grim Dawn, and adapts them to fit in our game’s unique loop. The core idea is very simple: there are [b]52 mini-skill-trees[/b] (Constellations), spread out in a huge “sky”. You start at the very center, and as you unlock and complete Constellations you get access to new ones further and further away from the center.[/p][p]
Constellations come in [b]7 different colors[/b], which are made by a combination of [b]3 base ones[/b], which we call “[b]Devotion Paths[/b]”: [b]Fury (Red)[/b], [b]Discipline (Green)[/b] and [b]Faith (Blue)[/b]. These Paths are roughly equivalent to classic RPG classes in terms of playstyle: [b]Warrior[/b], [b]Rogue[/b] and [b]Mage[/b], respectively.[/p][p][/p][p]Although early on you will need to choose one of these 3 Paths to focus on, as you gain more Constellation points you will have freedom to combine them in any way you choose, creating your own starting “class” every time you start a new Ascension.[/p][p]
Additionally, your choice of Devotion Path will influence the drop rates of certain Relics, and will unlock new Unique Relics as you progress, as we’ll explain in the next section.[/p][h2]
[b]Ascension Rewards[/b][/h2][p][/p][p]If you power through this harder challenge that you created for yourself and complete your Ascension, what do you get out of it?

[/p][p][img src="https://lh7-rt.googleusercontent.com/docsz/AD_4nXdxmsylBjWdh4aT5al7TKgeRcS1zdRMOb1NTxGF1u_W0WWePZSafLQ3JplsCZdNoo1YYp3ybwi0qWdciJ3ReyAaZ6vxyDhR3xrRrNFmuq6CJl_9DliR29JDs3sycEwt5L-8DLmUkw?key=VYjU1aVjpAbSZisEetooWg"][/img][/p][p]
The first thing is completing [b]Promises[/b]. These are achievements that will reward you with more starting Constellation points. Constellations are immensely powerful, so they will be key in allowing you to create builds that are powerful enough to conquer the later Hell levels.[/p][p][/p][p]You will also get access to [b]new Unique Relics[/b] that only appear in endgame, based on your Devotion Path choices. Some Unique Relics are more general-use, but some will be more related to Discipline, Faith or Fury builds. This means that changing your starting “class” will also affect the new Relics that  you will encounter during your endgame runs.[/p][p][/p][h2][b]What’s Coming Next?[/b][/h2][p]
For Ascension to leave Beta, we expect not only the overall balance of the builds, choices and difficulty to be much improved, but we’re also working on brand new features.[/p][p]
The first one will come soon after release in our free [b]“Clockmaker’s Tools” update: crafting[/b]! You will be able to find Crafting currency during your runs, and use them back in Quixeramobim to customize your Relics in many ways - adding, removing, improving affixes, and even “Corrupting” a Relic with wild possible results.[/p][p][/p][p]Most importantly, during Beta you will be replaying the same environments from the campaign, and fighting the same enemies and Bosses. It can be fun at first, but after dozens of hours of Ascension we expect you to grow a bit tired of it.[/p][p][/p][p]That’s why we are working on creating [b]12 new Biomes[/b] exclusively for Ascension, with remixed enemies and bosses from the campaign and from our upcoming expansion. We will talk more about that next week, so stay tuned![/p][h1]
Endgame Livestream Today!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/00ce7cfc5645092e595473d819d6900be74b1432.png"][/img][/h1][p][url="https://www.youtube.com/live/C3AvD_f029M"](52) Mark Venturelli, Game Director, Showcasing Hell Clock Endgame - YouTube[/url]

Today at 6PM BRT we’re going live on the [b]Hell Clock Brasil YouTube channel[/b] — and yes, the stream will be in [b]English[/b] so everyone in the community can join in! [/p][p][/p][p]I’ll walk you through the new endgame features, talk a bit about our design choices so far, how things work, and what you can expect from this wild journey. Don’t miss it!
[/p][p]That’s all we have for today. Thanks for taking the time to read this deep dive into Hell Clock’s first Endgame system. We can’t wait to get the full game in your hands on July 22nd![/p][p]

Cheers,
~ Mark[/p][p]
[/p][p][/p][h1][/h1]

notes.title: Same Devs. Different RPG. Still Full of Heart!
notes.content:
[p]Hey Clockmakers,[/p][p][/p][p]We’d like to take a moment to shine a little spotlight on a project that’s been very close to our hearts for a long time. While Hell Clock has been taking shape as our dark, historical ARPG with roguelike action, we’ve also been working hard on a second game, one that we feel deserves a second chance to be discovered by more players.[/p][p]
It’s called Relic Hunters Legend, and it's launching into 1.0 on [b]August 14[/b], just a few weeks after Hell Clock releases.

[/p][previewyoutube="wbhlLJNGjJ0;full"][/previewyoutube][p]

We know it might look very different at first glance, its colorful, cartoon-inspired style is far from the gritty tone of Hell Clock, but we truly believe that if you love deep RPG systems, custom builds, and a good underdog story, there’s something special waiting for you in Relic Hunters Legend.[/p][h1][b]
What is Relic Hunters Legend?
[/b][/h1][p]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/6ddaee5dabf4cbc0a91288d94be7309f0178938a.gif"][/img][/p][p]Relic Hunters Legend is a fast-paced looter shooter RPG with deep build customization, tight combat, and a heartfelt sci-fi story about friendship, rebellion, and stolen memories. You can play solo offline or team up with 4 friends in online co-op.
[/p][p]Over the years, the game has evolved massively, from a free-to-play project to a fully premium experience, and the 1.0 release is right around the corner! The 1.0  launch will introduce the final chapter of the main story campaign, a new region with additional missions, revamped cosmetics unlocking, increased storage space, and a new Steam achievement. The game will offer approximately[b] 30 hours of story content[/b] and over [b]200 hours of gameplay [/b]for those aiming for full completion.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/9ccfadfb6a3ef7de7f43f1a8ede25a34f3be499a.jpg"][/img]

[b]Key Features[/b][/p][list][*][p]Play Solo or 4-player online co-op gameplay[/p][/*][*][p][b]Over 200 collectible items[/b]—including legendary weapons, gear, and relics. Built to support bold theorycrafting, synergy-chasing, and power-hunting.[/p][/*][*][p]Voiced campaign with [b]30+ hours [/b]of story across 3 Acts and [b]200 hours for full completion[/b][/p][/*][*][p][b]Nine Game Modes[/b] and 30+ handcrafted maps[/p][/*][*][p]Offline play with local saves and full Steam Cloud sync[/p][/*][*][p]Launching with its [b]full original soundtrack
[/b][/p][/*][/list][h1][b]
What Hell Clock and Relic Hunters Legend Share
[/b][/h1][p]At first glance, these games might seem like opposites. One is a haunting roguelike based on real Brazilian history, and the other is a vibrant sci-fi adventure. But underneath the aesthetics, they share the same [b]DNA[/b].[/p][p][/p][list][*][p]Both games are built around meaningful progression, deep build crafting, and tight action combat.[/p][/*][*][p]Both were made by a small team who love RPGs and care about doing things differently.[/p][/*][*][p]And both are shaped by player feedback, tough development decisions, and a desire to tell stories that matter.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]If you’ve enjoyed diving into the mechanics and freedom of Hell Clock, there’s a real chance you’ll find something to love in Relic Hunters Legend too.


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/0eb6996f29faff4d7634b226b0a84c47bc8832b0.png"][/img][/p][h1][b]
Thank You, From All of Us at Rogue Snail[/b][/h1][p]
We can’t express enough how grateful we are for the love and support we’ve received on Hell Clock so far. Launching two games in such a short time is no small feat, but it’s only possible because of this amazing community.
[/p][p]Our two most ambitious RPGs are launching just weeks apart, and we hope you’ll enjoy both journeys, each with its own unique tone, challenges, and heart.
 [/p][p]Thanks for sticking with us, and we’ll see you soon in both Canudos… and the stars. ✨[/p][p]
[/p][p]With love,[/p][p]— The Rogue Snail Team 🐌[/p][p]
[/p]

notes.title: New Launch Date + New Demo
notes.content:
[b]Attention Clockmakers[/b], we have two big updates to share:

[b]We have made the decision to shift the launch date for Hell Clock from June 18 to July 22.  We’ve also today updated the Hell Clock demo with new content. [/b]

Why are we shifting to July? The main reason is the new Path of Exile league (3.26) dropping on June 13. It's bittersweet because as players we are very excited that our favorite game will have an update after a long time... but as indie developers of a small ARPG we simply cannot compete with a huge launch like that, so we are forced to delay.

The launch of Hell Clock is critical for our studio. We don't really get a second chance at this. And although June 18th was a perfect timing (right next to Steam Next Fest!), we hope that July 22nd will give us a fair shot at reaching ARPG and roguelike fans around the world.

We’re all big fans and PoE players, and it had a huge influence on the development of Hell Clock. We think it’s best to give Hell Clock some breathing room from that, let you guys (and our team) enjoy the new season, and then dive into Hell Clock a bit later. 

On the plus side, this also gives us a bit more time to work on our endgame system, Ascension, which will be available as a Beta at launch in July. Previously, our plan was [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ji-sO68H1-8]to launch Ascension a few weeks after launch[/url]. 

For today, here’s what’s new in the demo:
[list][*] More Hell - The demo has been extended from 14 to 17 floors. 
[*] English is in - Full English language voice over is now in the demo. 
[*] Chinese localization - Full text localization in simplified Chinese is now available. 
[*] Progression carries over - From here on out, there will be no further progression wipe. Any progress you make in the demo will carry over to launch.

notes.title: How We Make Progression Fun in our ARPG
notes.content:
Hey everyone,

My name is Mark, and I'm one of the game designers working on Hell Clock. We’re super happy with all the positive reactions to our Demo, and a lot of you have been mentioning the speed, the “power surges”, and just how fun it feels to progress in the game. So today I wanted to give you a peek behind the curtain and talk about our design philosophy around progression and difficulty.

I started seriously researching progression design in 2017, for [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/633080/Relic_Hunters_Legend/]Relic Hunters Legend[/url]. I had always been a big RPG gamer, but I wanted to REALLY dissect progression. Every single game these days slaps some kind of progression system, and 99% of the time it feels tacked-on and shallow compared to the “real” ones such as [b]Diablo 2[/b].

So I took a deep dive into this subject, and analyzed dozens of games, both good and bad, to see what makes progression systems “tick”.

And what I discovered is that the satisfying feeling of power has absolutely [b]NOTHING[/b] to do with how [b]difficult[/b] or[b] easy[/b] a game is. But it has [b]EVERYTHING[/b] to do with [b]pacing[/b].

--

[h1]Difficulty Means Nothing[/h1]

If you are constantly feeling stronger than the enemies, the game is boring. If you are constantly feeling weaker than the enemies, the game is also boring. This is also one of the many reasons why games where enemies scale automatically to match player level feel so bland.

Good progression is a kind of[b] storytelling[/b]. It needs to have drama. Ups and downs. You need to struggle a bit, then overcome the struggle, even feel invincible for a while, but then realize that there are even bigger challenges out there which will humble you - but will also fuel your desire to overcome them!

I’m a visual thinker, so let’s try and visualize what I’ve just said:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/d2c993e2534f62d1bab6b129a309b8eba1e4dd93.png[/img]

In this graph we see two boring games: in game “A” (Blue) you feel constantly underpowered, and defeating enemies always feels like a struggle. In game “B” (Red) it’s the opposite: you constantly feel OP and enemies are a joke. Although these two hypothetical games might seem very different, the end result is the same: they are boring us asleep.

Now let’s see how an ideal game might look like compared to these two:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/4e72f83e7fb16d149d688ba08ac59a4b60088f8e.png[/img]

You can already see how much more dynamic this looks. And if it reminds you of a rollercoaster, that’s no coincidence: rollercoasters are a literal, physical representation of this basic principle of all entertainment. Hills and valleys. Ups and downs. Struggling and overcoming.

[h1]Our Model[/h1]

We designed Hell Clock with a model that embodies this idea of dynamic progression. We don’t have a catchy name for it (or any name at all, actually), so we just refer to it as the [b]“Climb, Wall, Breakthrough and Payoff”[/b] model.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/ca07f209d0b5799c20016ef370547a2de7ca929e.png[/img]

[b]“The Climb” [/b]describes a moment where we feel like the enemies’ power is slowly and steadily creeping in on ours. We are still capable of defeating the obstacles, but it feels like they are getting more difficult faster than we are getting stronger. In the Demo, you can see this in action on the first floors.

[b]“The Wall” [/b]is when the build-up from the Climb reaches its climax: either a boss fight, a new enemy type, a new area, a new mechanic, SOMETHING is introduced that suddenly makes us feel vulnerable and weak, like all of our power means nothing. In our Demo, you might feel this the first time you meet Bosses like The Jailer, or The Merchant and when you reach the Caves biome.

But wait, we don’t ragequit yet, because here comes [b]“The Breakthrough”[/b]: a missing piece that was JUST out of reach before, but is now ours. It could be a new item, a new skill, a new piece of information, anything that can give us an edge. In the Hell Clock Demo, this is the first power spike you get from your Blessed Weapon, or The Great Bell, or your first Unique Relic.

Then it is finally time for [b]“The Payoff”[/b], our just reward for our struggles, when we get to feel untouchable, like we just “solved” or even “broke” the game, and everything that felt challenging before is now trivialized. In the Demo, that’s when you get to blast through the levels and melt in seconds some of the Bosses who were giving you trouble in previous runs.

But of course, the cycle has to restart, so we slowly start to feel like [b]“The Climb”[/b] is setting in again…

[h1]Models Are Not Recipes[/h1]

But of course, while all of this sounds great in theory, it is far from trivial to implement in practice. And every game comes with its own quirks and challenges, so what works for us might not work for another game, and vice-versa.

So far, from the reception we got for the Hell Clock Demo, it seems you enjoy this approach - at least for the duration of a small Demo, of course.

Our challenge now is to give you the same feeling over the entire campaign! But we are confident that as long as we keep playing the game a lot, listening to your feedback, and willing to change what isn’t working in our game, we will get there.

[h3]TL:DR - Always easy bad. Always hard bad. Rollercoaster good.[/h3]

Thanks a lot for reading! 

Cheers,
~ Mark

notes.title: Demo Patch #1 is Live!
Demo Update – Major Improvements, Gamepad Support & New Systems!
notes.content:
Hey Clockmakers,

Releasing our first Playtest last year was an amazing experience! We were honestly surprised that, even though bad luck had us revealing our ARPG a mere DAY before the biggest ARPG launch of recent memory, we still got a LOT of interest in our game, and a lot of useful feedback.

For this new Demo, we've made significant changes to several systems. Our goal is to improve the early game experience and lay the foundation for the endgame systems that are in development.

We also focused on the main area of feedback from December: [b]controls[/b]. We have polished the WASD-movement experience, and properly implemented gamepad support. The gamepad support is still not 100% final quality, so please let us know if you encounter any difficulties or frustrations.

[b]Here’s the breakdown of what we’ve changed:[/b]

[h1]Game Experience Improvements[/h1]

[h2]Improved WASD and Gamepad Controls[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/4c8061eb374a0c002d1ed3715cd91f372816018d.gif[/img]

[b]Your Feedback: [/b]WASD control scheme had inconsistencies and quality of life issues. Also, Gamepad control was placeholder and did not work on menu screens.

[b]Our Solution:[/b] We replaced our "band-aid" control scheme with a polished version. We also officially implemented gamepad support, and everything should be working fine and dandy now (with the exception of the Reliquary screen, which is usable but is still a work-in-progress - it also needs quite a bit of polish for mouse/keyboard as well).

[h2]Less Oppressive Clock Timer[/h2]

[b]Your Feedback:[/b] Clock always ticking down can feel oppressive/unrewarding.

[b]Our Solution:[/b] We introduced a new in-game drop that adds more Time to the current run’s clock. You are also guaranteed to get +90 seconds from the main Bosses of each Act.

[h2]Better Item Pickup and Loot Behavior[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/27c558e5dc5b2e51f7a0cb5f34bc4f893a73e70b.gif[/img]

[b]Your Feedback:[/b] Sometimes it was annoying to pick up items as a melee build or when blasting quickly through the level. Also, chests took too long to drop their loot and it felt like a waste of precious clock seconds.

[b]Our Solution:[/b] We made adjustments to how item drops behave: when you open chests, all items will automatically be attracted to you after they finish dropping (you don’t need to stand next to the chest). Now, this logic also applies to loot from enemies: if you are near the enemy when it dies, the loot will automatically be attracted to you. The only case where loot will stay on the floor is if you kill enemies from a range and never get close.

[h2]Skill Synergies and Build Diversity[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/dccc59e93d3bd5f427c2b2db751058e0006c43d0.gif[/img]

[b]Your Feedback: [/b]The game rewards/incentivizes you for including just a few Skills on your bar.

[b]Our Solution: [/b]We introduced a new "Skill Synergies" system which provides passive benefits for ranking up any skill; we have also made the Blessings Deck smaller, and you now have less level-ups per run overall - which means you’ll run out of upgrades sooner if you take only a few skills. ​

[i]Designer Note: It's still a viable option to take only a few Skills if you don’t plan to do deeper than 7-9 Floors in a given run - but now it’s a viable choice instead of always being the optimal play.[/i]

[h2]More Meaningful Blessings and Upgrades[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/8b789acd5b63a32860f4f74021626976cf490bf9.gif[/img]

[b]Your Feedback:[/b] Picking up a "Common" level-up Blessing felt bad.

[b]Our Solution: [/b]Our new Blessings balance "squashed" stats and made every upgrade more meaningful; Common and Magic Blessings are now more powerful across the board, and the gap to Rares and Uniques is now less jarring.

[h2]Smoother Game Flow with Fewer Level-Up Interruptions[/h2]

[b]Your Feedback:[/b] Too many level-ups interrupted the flow of the game, especially in deeper floors.

[b]Our Solution: [/b]We made a new XP Curve with drastically less level-ups per run, especially at the high-end. Our new Blessings balance also means each level up is more meaningful than before, so you still feel that power surge, just with less interruptions.

[h2]Balanced Gold Costs and Upgrade Depth[/h2]

[b]Your Feedback: [/b]Gold costs for upgrades sometimes were too expensive / felt random. They also felt a bit shallow/simplistic.

[b]Our Solution:[/b] We introduced a completely new "Blessings of Foundation" system, which gives consistent and player-controlling price scaling, as well as raised the skill ceiling of the game from the very first run. This is a complicated feature to explain briefly, so check our in-depth explanation below if you’re interested!

[h2]New Skill Levels and Mana Rework[/h2]

[b]Your Feedback: [/b]Mana quickly becomes meaningless and overall doesn’t feel good.

[b]Our Solution: [/b] We have introduced a new "Skill Level" system. You can unlock new Skill Levels at the Great Bell, which gives you the choice to use more powerful versions of Skills - but at higher Mana costs.

[i]Designer Note: This system has PLACEHOLDER UI and will be clunky and weird to use in this Demo, we apologize for that, but we wanted to push this out as soon as possible even in this crude state.[/i]

[h2]More Unique Relics Early On[/h2]

[b]Your Feedback:[/b] Unique Relics are really cool but there could be more of them early on.

[b]Our Solution:[/b] Just for the Demo, we have unlocked all of the Act 1 Unique Relics on the drop pool. This might make your first runs a bit more RNG-heavy than intended, but provide much more choice and exciting build opportunities.

For the final game, we are currently planning to stick to limiting Unique Relic drop pools early on, and increase it as you progress (this is intended to guide newer players so they are not overwhelmed with choice and/or frustrated with bad RNG). But rest assured that the endgame “Hell Mode” will have a huge Relic drop pool. We plan to ship the game with over 100 Uniques, and keep adding more post-launch based on your feedback.

Also, we've finished fleshing out our Ailments system (which was not a "Feedback" reported by you, but it's still a significant improvement! pats own back).

[h1]New Feature: "Blessings of Foundation"[/h1]

We have replaced the old Gold Totem upgrades with a new tiered system with different categories.

All upgrades and prices start the run at the lowest level, so you won’t see super-expensive stuff right away. By purchasing a Blessing, you will unlock one or more possible upgrades in the same category, so you are in control of how expensive your new Totems will be.

There are[b] six Blessings of Foundation categories[/b]:

[list]
[*] [b]Precision:[/b] upgrades related to Critical Chance, Critical Damage and Projectiles.
[*] [b]Force:[/b] upgrades related to Elemental Damage, Elemental Ailments and Area of Effect.
[*] [b]Constitution:[/b] upgrades related to Life, Life Regen, Endurance and Healing.
[*] [b]Lethality:[/b] upgrades related to Physical damage, Melee and Bleed.
[*] [b]Spirit:[/b] upgrades related to Mana, Cooldown Reduction, Mana Shield and Conviction.
[*] [b]Alacrity:[/b] upgrades related to Move Speed, Attack Speed and Evasion.
[/list]

This is a map of how you progress through each Foundation category (we plan to make it available in-game in the near future):

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45331821/395d23b10e41075aef0532e9dbe1a1acc6ac2db1.png[/img]

[h1]Upcoming Feature: English Voiceover![/h1]

We’re happy to announce that with the backing of Mad Mushroom we’ve hired some talented voice talent to do a full English dub of the game. It will be done in time for release later this year, so you will have the option of playing the game either in the original Brazilian Portuguese or the English dub.

[h1]Thanks And Have Fun![/h1]

Thank you so much for your support! We hope to hear more from you, and make the game the best it can be for release.

If you have any (constructive and respectful) feedback, we LOVE to hear it! You can leave it here on the Steam Community, or join our [url=http://Discord.gg/HellClockGame]Discord channel[/url] - whichever you prefer!
